evidenceDependencyAnalysis.why: Before proposing that any class be retired, the lane close artifacts were checked for citations INTO _inbox, because a close artifact whose evidence file has been deleted becomes an unverifiable claim.
evidenceDependencyAnalysis.method: grep -rhoE '_inbox/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+\.(log|json)' over _inbox/*_close.json and _inbox/*_close.md, deduplicated, then each cited path existence-checked on disk.
evidenceDependencyAnalysis.keyResult: Close artifacts cite SUMMARY JSON almost exclusively. Of 114 distinct cited artifacts, exactly ONE is a writer-run .log (2026-08-06_T1_elgin_apply_1256277.log). The other 113 are .json summaries. This is the empirical basis for the retention rule: the raw .log corpus is 892 files but carries only 1 inbound evidence citation, whereas the .json summary layer is what closes actually depend on.

inboxRetentionRuleProposal.framing: Proposed as a RULE for operator ruling, not a file-by-file retirement list. Nothing was moved, retired, or deleted by this pass. The rule is keyed on CLASS first and age second, because the population is back-loaded (74.8% of dated files are from the current half-month) and an age-only rule would be nearly inert.
inboxRetentionRuleProposal.rule: R1 - SWEEP RAW WRITER-RUN LOGS BY WAVE. A file in _inbox/ top level is eligible for archival move (never deletion) into _inbox/<lane>_<wave>_archive/ when ALL FOUR hold: (a) its name matches _(dry|dryrun|apply|apply[0-9]+)\.(log|txt)$; (b) it is UNTRACKED in git; (c) its lane has a corresponding _close.md or _close.json present in _inbox/; and (d) its path is not cited by any close artifact. R2 - NEVER SWEEP the four protected classes: *_close.*, *_STATUS.md, README.md, and any file cited by a close artifact. R3 - LEAVE ALL .json ALONE in this pass; the summary-JSON layer is what closes depend on (113 of 114 citations) and needs its own separate ruling. R4 - the 11 underscore-prefixed working files get an explicit operator ruling each, because their provenance cannot be inferred from their names.
inboxRetentionRuleProposal.rationale: The evidence-dependency scan is the whole argument. The raw .log corpus is the largest class in the directory (892 files recursive, 18.4 MB, the biggest byte consumer) and it is the class the close artifacts do NOT depend on - exactly 1 inbound citation across 114. Meanwhile the close artifacts themselves are 158-of-214 tracked, i.e. already committed as durable evidence, and the .json summaries they cite are 113-of-114 present. The repo has already voted with its index: logs were never committed (834 of 892 untracked), summaries and closes were. The rule makes that existing implicit policy explicit. Crucially, this action has ALREADY BEEN PERFORMED ONCE BY HAND: _inbox/wave3_attempt1_archive holds exactly 241 untracked L2 wave-3 dry/apply1/apply2 logs swept wholesale into an archive subdir. R1 generalizes a precedent the operator already set rather than inventing new policy.

whatItWouldRetire.estimatedFiles: Approximately 600-640 top-level raw .log/.txt writer-run files, being the 649 top-level matches minus the ~58 tracked ones and minus the 1 cited log. Exact figure must be recomputed at execution time against the then-current index, not taken from this artifact.
whatItWouldRetire.action: MOVE into _inbox/<lane>_<wave>_archive/, mirroring the existing wave3_attempt1_archive. NOT deletion. Nothing leaves the working tree.
whatItWouldRetire.byteRecovery: None from git (they were never committed). The gain is navigability: top-level _inbox drops from 2,276 to roughly 1,650, and the close/STATUS/summary layer stops being buried under a 3:1 majority of raw run logs.

whatItWouldKeep.allJson: All 903 .json - including the 254 t6_cad_probe files (253 tracked) and every cited summary. Deferred to a separate ruling.

risks: HIGH - Grep-based recovery breaks. Agents and the planner locate prior run evidence by grepping _inbox/ flat. Moving 600+ files into archive subdirs is safe for grep -r but breaks any tooling that globs _inbox/*.log at exactly one level. Mitigation: audit scripts/ for single-level _inbox globs BEFORE executing R1. This audit was NOT performed by this pass and is a prerequisite.

HIGH - Untracked means unrecoverable. 834 of the 892 logs are untracked, so a mistaken move has no git undo. This is precisely why R1 specifies MOVE and never delete, and why it must run as one reviewable batch rather than incrementally.

MEDIUM - Lane-to-close matching is a heuristic. Clause (c) infers a lane from the filename token (L2_WAVE1, T1, l19). Filename lane tokens are inconsistently cased and formed across the corpus. A lane whose close was written to _sessions/ rather than _inbox/ would fail clause (c) and be wrongly retained - a safe failure direction, but R1 under-sweeps rather than over-sweeps.

MEDIUM - The citation scan covered close artifacts only. Files cited from _decisions/, _sessions/, 90_operations/, or OPS-17 itself were NOT scanned. A log cited from a canonical doc outside _inbox would be missed. Mitigation: widen the citation grep repo-wide before executing.
LOW - The 16 gitignored PDFs sit inside subdirs already and are untouched by R1.

PROCESS - R1 treats a symptom. The root cause is that the README declared sweep (deletes the inbox file once filed) is not being executed at all. Adopting R1 without restoring sweep discipline means _inbox regrows at the current rate of roughly 1,494 files per half-month.
inboxRetentionRuleProposal.recommendation: Adopt R2 and R3 immediately as standing protections - they cost nothing and prevent the dangerous mistake. Adopt R1 only after the two prerequisite audits (single-level _inbox globs in scripts/; repo-wide citation grep) come back clean. R4 needs an operator ruling on 11 named files and can be done in one pass. Separately and independently of all four: fix the L16 roll-up gap, and commit the 4 untracked _sessions/ summaries.

The _inbox courier protocol is declared but not executed. _inbox/README.md (status active) states the planner deletes the inbox file once filed and that a non-empty _inbox/ at session start means there is uncouriered work to file before anything else. The directory holds 2,276 top-level files spanning 2026-05-25 to 2026-08-14. The sweep-and-delete half of the protocol has not run in the ~12 weeks the directory has existed. Root cause of _inbox size; any retention rule adopted without restoring the sweep only buys time.

Close artifacts depend on the JSON summary layer, not on raw logs. Of 114 distinct _inbox artifacts cited by close files, 113 are .json and exactly 1 is a .log. Yet .log is the largest class (892 recursive, 18.4 MB) and the least committed (834 of 892 untracked). This asymmetry is the empirical justification for the proposed retention rule and is the single most decision-relevant finding of this pass.

BROKEN EVIDENCE CHAIN - L16 has no roll-up close. Four leg-close artifacts (l16_leg0_sd_residue_close.json, l16_leg1_rail_corridor_close.json, l16_leg2_harris_parcel_node_close.json, l16_mud_scorer_close.json) each cite _inbox/2026-08-13_l16_close.json, which does not exist anywhere in _inbox. _dispatches and _sessions need no retention rule at all. Both are ~2.5 MB, 100% .md, and near-100% convention-compliant (_dispatches 326/327 date-prefixed with the one exception being the declared template; _sessions 226/227). Recommend repo_map.md mark both keep-forever. All cleanup attention belongs on _inbox and _scratch.

The four directories divide cleanly by owner and write-path, which repo_map.md should record: _dispatches is planner-WRITE / fleet-READ (work orders out); _inbox is fleet-WRITE / planner-READ (evidence in); _sessions is planner-WRITE (durable narrative); _scratch is fleet-WRITE / fleet-READ (working memory, explicitly non-durable). Confusion between _inbox and _scratch is the likeliest failure mode for the four incoming build lanes: both take agent-written mid-work files, but _inbox output is evidence the planner will act on while _scratch output is disposable.
